new_statements.quote: [KULR 25, p. 43] Each vowel quality is stable ([i, e, a, o, u]), and each acoustic space is independently distributed in F1-F2 coordinate. Suprasegmental cues, such as loudness, pitch, etc., serve only as boundary markers of words, phrases, etc. [AALL 6, p. 29] A morpho-syntactic word in Kadorih can be defined using prosodic criteria in (2). (2) a. No obvious pause ... can divide a word into smaller segments. b. The word may carry a single intonation or be part of a structure which carries a single intonation. c. Within a single intonation unit, a falling pitch can occur only in its last syllable. ... this tetrasyllabic structure (mo. so. mo. som) cannot be separated into moso and mosom, and a falling pitch occurs only in its last syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kadorih has no contrastive word stress: loudness and pitch function only demarcatively, marking word and phrase boundaries. The one word-level pitch event described is a fall confined to the final syllable of the prosodic word / intonation unit (also realised on word-final diphthongs, Inagaki 2005: 38-39); no rule assigning stress to a particular syllable is stated anywhere in the accessible corpus.
new_statements.exceptions: None as such. Repeated (as opposed to reduplicated) outputs form two prosodic words and may carry two intonations with a pitch fall elsewhere than the last syllable (AALL 6 p. 29-30). Inagaki 2007 notes preaspirated /hT/ only before the final-syllable nucleus; Inagaki 2015 notes boundary-related lengthening of word-final vowels in discourse.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern the prosodic word and intonation unit as boundary-marked domains (demarcative prominence), based on wordlists (~2500 items), texts and elicitation recorded in Tumbang Marikoi 2005-2006; pitch fall described for citation-form words ending an intonation unit (e.g. bau 'mouth' vs pambau 'window' F0 curves in the 2005 paper).
new_statements.identity_note: Inagaki's works describe Kadorih (= Dohoi = Ot Danum, glottocode otda1235 / ISO otd) as spoken in Tumbang Marikoi on the upper Kahayan River, Central Kalimantan (fieldwork 2005-2006). Martina et al. 2005 describes 'Bahasa Dayak Uud Danum' of West Kalimantan (Serawai/Ambalau, Sintang), the western variety catalogued under the same ISO code otd. Taib et al. 1990 pools speakers from five kecamatan in Central Kalimantan.

sources.citation: Inagaki, Kazuya. 2011. Word duplication in Kadorih. Asian and African Languages and Linguistics (AALL) 6: 27-44.
sources.note: p. 29, prosodic criteria for the word: (2c) 'Within a single intonation unit, a falling pitch can occur only in its last syllable'; reduplicated mosomosom 'a falling pitch occurs only in its last syllable'; repeated outputs may carry two intonations. Word-final pitch fall as the word/IU-level prosodic event; no 'stress' terminology.

sources.citation: Inagaki, Kazuya. 2008. Kadori-go: Boruneo-tou no oosutoroneshia-kei gengo no kijutsu [Kadorih: the description of an Austronesian language of Borneo]. PhD thesis, Kyoto University. (KURENAI hdl:2433/124167 = 9-page abstract and examiners' report only)
sources.note: Only the abstract/report is online (scanned, Japanese). It says ch. 1 surveys 'segments, syllable structure, suprasegmental features' typologically and ch. 2 (phonology) establishes phonemes, diphthong conditions, syllable types V/CV/VC/VV/CVC/CVV and a disyllabic minimal prosodic word; no statement of stress placement in the summary. Full 333-page thesis not accessible.

sources.citation: Inagaki, Kazuya. 2007. Kadori-go ni okeru gochuu no heisaon to hasatsuon [Word-medial stops and affricates in Kadorih]. Gengo Kenkyu 132: 111-120. doi:10.11435/gengo.132.0_111
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent; observes that preaspirated /-hT-/ occurs only immediately before the word-final syllable nucleus (V2_V1).

sources.citation: Inagaki, Kazuya. 2005. Phonemic sketch of Dohoi/Kadorih (Austronesian: upper reaches of Kahayan River in Kalimantan, Indonesia). Kyoto University Linguistic Research 24: 15-43. doi:10.14989/87858
sources.note: No stress/accent section. Sec. 3.2 (pp. 38-39): string-final diphthongs carry a falling pitch (high on first element, low on second); non-final or non-high-second vowel sequences show a slight fall starting at the second element; supported by F0 curves (Fig. 8). Nothing on which syllable is stressed.

sources.citation: Martina; Hari Purwiati; Musfeptial. 2005. Morfologi Bahasa Dayak Uud Danum. Pontianak: Balai Bahasa Provinsi Kalimantan Barat (Pusat Bahasa, Depdiknas). 110 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.2.1, p. 22: 'Akan tetapi bahasa Dayak Uud Danum hanya dibentuk dengan fonem segmental saja... status kata... sepenuhnya ditentukan oleh fonem segmental' -- i.e. no suprasegmental (stress) phonemes; no placement rule. West Kalimantan Uud Danum variety.
